clue.text: Latvian capital has party — no going back to dance

parts.note: Riga is the capital city of Latvia
a do is an informal word for a party

indicators.note: going back tells us the word no is read from right to left

explanation.surface: Someone in Riga throws a party but refuses to retreat onto the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns NO into ON, which ends the answer after RIGA and DO. 'has' is only a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigadoon is a lively old Provençal folk dance for couples.

explanation.surface: A plea to turn down junk.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline is the verb sense; waste or garbage is the noun, pronounced differently.

clue.text: Medico in bad weather takes — a risk

indicators.note: in places the doctor's letters within the word for bad weather

parts.note: a gale is a spell of stormy weather
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor setting out in a storm is taking a chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts MB inside GALE; 'takes' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamble is a venture whose outcome is uncertain, a chance taken.

indicators.note: leading picks out the letter at the front of dealer
rare meat is undercooked, so felt is reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A top antiques dealer judged a piece of pottery unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' gives D and 'rare' rearranges FELT into ELFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is the blue-and-white tin-glazed pottery made in the Dutch town of that name.

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, a nil score shaped like O
a ration is a fixed share

explanation.surface: A romantic urged to share this address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'this' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal public address.

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a banquet longer.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen or stretch out is one sense; a lavish meal laid out on the table is the other.

clue.text: Gentle inhabitant becomes" chief of state

parts.note: P, for piano, is the musical marking for soft or gentle
a resident is an inhabitant

explanation.surface: A mild local rises to lead the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the elected head of a republic.

clue.text: Harsh demand once start of play is on

parts.note: ex means former, what something once was
a film director calls out action to begin a scene

explanation.surface: A tough requirement used to apply when a match began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is on' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaction is a severe or unfair levy insisted upon, such as an extortionate tax.

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
an array is an impressive display

explanation.surface: A show staged in Hades leads to chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causes' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Disarray is a state of disorder or muddle.

clue.text: Well known member of a pope's household

explanation.surface: A celebrated figure who lives in the Vatican.
explanation.definitionFit: Something often seen is recognisable; historically, a servant or officer living in a pope's or bishop's household carried that title too.

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold a guest, so the friends' word holds the journalist's inside it

parts.note: pals are friends
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Going on bike rides with mates who are hosting a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' puts ED inside PALS. 'Cycles' is a verb here, as in pedals along.
explanation.definitionFit: To pedal is to ride a bicycle, working its foot levers.

clue.text: Time at school for technical expression.

explanation.surface: A school period described with jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: A school year divides into teaching periods; a specialist word or phrase is the other meaning.

clue.text: Game- I lost 'stupidly by — the river

indicators.note: doing something stupidly means doing it in a muddled way, so the letters of I and lost are jumbled

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A player confesses to losing a game foolishly beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' rearranges I LOST into SOLIT, and AIRE (a Yorkshire river) follows; 'by' only places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitaire is a one-player game, played with cards or with pegs on a board.

explanation.surface: An instruction to put people in one grave.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury is to lay a body in the ground; inter- is also a Latin-derived prefix for between or among, things mutually joined.

explanation.surface: A newly harnessed team of two horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Spick and span means clean and new, so fresh; in American usage a matched team of two harnessed horses or mules is also called this.

parts.note: someone carried along on a journey without doing the work, and in a team a member who does not pull their weight

explanation.surface: A lazy tourist.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a team member who does no work is said to be carried along like a rider in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider in a vehicle who is not driving does nothing, so a slacker in a team gets the same name.

clue.text: Mole may turn into a tumour

indicators.note: turn into means change shape, so the letters of mole and may are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that a skin mole could become cancerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn into' rearranges MOLE and MAY, seven letters, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Myeloma is a malignant growth of the bone marrow's plasma cells.

parts.note: a crusade is a campaign for a cause

explanation.surface: A warmonger campaigns for the right wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Crusaders were medieval Christian soldiers fighting holy wars, so a warrior for a cause.

explanation.surface: Anglers' bait that tempts cricket players.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolving baits that flash in water are one sense; slow bowlers who turn the ball are the other, in cricket, England's bat-and-ball summer game.

parts.note: 26-down is a word for quick, so the clue asks for a quick answer given back

explanation.surface: A cross-referenced phrase for a snappy comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: The number points at 26-down, a word meaning quick, so read the clue as 'quick reply'.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a swift, sharp retort, borrowed from a fencer's quick counter-thrust.

indicators.note: some means only part of the words let children is used

explanation.surface: Some kids allowed to engrave patterns in metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals letters taken from inside 'let children'.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to cut a pattern into metal with acid.

clue.text: Girl going to hospital for course

parts.note: Pat is a girl's name
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A young woman heads to hospital for treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' only joins PAT and H.
explanation.definitionFit: A path is a route or track followed, the way a course is.

explanation.surface: A request to provide groceries.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide or yield is the verb; fruit and vegetables grown for market are the noun.

parts.note: bi- is the prefix meaning two
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A pair of soldiers discovers an old ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'find' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bireme was an ancient galley with two banks of oars.

clue.text: Wine from Irish county to taste first

parts.note: Clare is a county in the west of Ireland

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of taste

explanation.surface: A drink from the west of Ireland to sample before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links; 'first' takes T from 'taste'.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux.

clue.text: After that 'time, it is wrong going to church

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing, the thing that is wrong
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Since that moment, attending church has been considered a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' joins SIN and CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Since means from a stated moment onwards, a time-adverb synonym.

parts.note: cross means annoyed or angry
a bill is an invoice

explanation.surface: A musician is irritated by the bill sent to them.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Music maker' is a songbird, not a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossbill is a finch, and songbirds are a crossword's makers of music.

explanation.surface: A fast author.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift means fast; Jonathan Swift wrote Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Doctor' tense seeing mechanical device in water

parts.note: edge is a state of tension, as in an edge to a voice

explanation.surface: A nervous doctor spots a machine in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeing' only joins the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dredge is a machine that scoops mud and silt from a river or harbour bed.

clue.text: He rebels noticing Greek: character always: after. money

indicators.note: after puts the word for always behind the word for money

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
tin is old slang for money
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A man in revolt notices a Greek always pursuing cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places EER (e'er) behind TIN, and MU starts the answer; 'noticing' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutineer is someone who rises against authority, especially on a ship.

explanation.surface: An instruction to travel to a holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn to something for help is one sense, as in a last resort; a holiday town is the other.

clue.text: Aware tennis team played, but not early

indicators.note: played suggests letters performing in a fresh order, signalling an anagram
but not tells us to leave out the letters for early from the fodder

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, marks the morning, the early part of the day

explanation.surface: A tennis side that was alert in its match, though not at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes AM (early, as in a.m.) from TENNIS TEAM, leaving TENNISTE; 'played' rearranges those eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentient means able to perceive and feel, conscious of surroundings.
